chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and Ibn Fazzal, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
No two believers meet at all except that the superior of the two is the one who loves his brother more intensely.

key_terms.أَشَدَّهُمَا: The more intense of the two

ai.seo_question: How is spiritual superiority among believers determined according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (as) links spiritual rank directly to the intensity of mutual affection, reflecting the Shia concept that love (mawadda) is a manifestation of faith. It implies that the quality of one's connection to the Divine is measured by the depth of their bond with fellow believers, a principle central to the theology of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, and Ibn Fazzal, from Safwan Al Jammal, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
No two ‘Momineen’ (Believers) would meet at all except that the superior of the two would be with more intense love for his brother’.
en.sarwar: 15. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn abu Nasr and ibn Faddal from Safwan al-Jammal from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Of the two believers who meet each other, the more meritorious one is the one who loves his brethren more intensely.”
